gap: No result ChatGPT got states that TerraMaster's own US store sells its 16 GB DDR5 NAS memory module for $469.99, which is more than its whole F4-425 4-bay NAS ($429.99), so a home buyer should get the RAM they need in the box rather than plan to upgrade it later.
standout_why: I compared against Starry Hope's 'Best 4-Bay NAS' and 'Best Synology Alternatives' pages (both cited, dated 2026-11-02), nasdrives.ca (cited) and our own current page. Starry Hope gives early-November list prices and a reason each model loses, but no RAM upgrade costs and no warranty lengths. Its prices are also now stale: DXP4800 Plus $656.99 against $619.99 today, DXP4800 GT $659.99 against $559.99 today, F4-425 Plus $599.99/$649.99 against $539.99 today. nasdrives.ca gives no NAS prices at all. ChatGPT's cards show B&H, Newegg and UGREEN prices but never the cost of adding memory. thisping.com would not load (TLS certificate error), so I couldn't check it.
decides: This backs the DXP4800 Plus as the pick at $619.99 on UGREEN's store today, $19 under the QNAP TS-464 ($639.00 on QNAP's store, with a 2–4 week lead time). It also says the RAM in the box matters. The DS925+ ships with 4 GB (Starry Hope), and TerraMaster's first-party 16 GB stick costs more than its entry NAS, so if Docker or Plex is likely, the TerraMaster F4-425 Pro (16 GB DDR5 included, $699.99) or the DXP4800 Plus (8 GB) beats buying a 4 GB box and upgrading it. Two price changes are worth adding to the page: the DXP4800 GT is now $559.99, $60 under the Plus, and the DH4300 Plus is $373.99 as the budget card.
